goal.goal: A city wants to compare daily PM2.5 concentrations from low-cost optical monitors at a humid coastal site and a drier inland site. Its monitors have not been checked together. From published field measurements, which comparisons, if any, could the city reasonably defend, and what should it do before ranking these neighborhoods? Give a quantitative result, its field conditions and the original source for the most consequential part of your advice.

report_delivery_receipts.rationale: Keep the two commissioned reviews in view and publish the provisional city-specific conclusion. The Addis Ababa original used two reference sites to calibrate hourly readings, then calculated spatial divergence between pairs of optical monitors. Its pooled hourly test error cannot set a threshold for a daily coastal–inland difference. West Philadelphia provides a directly checked daily gravimetric comparison at one site. Peñuelas shows that excluding humid readings changes both between-unit precision and coverage. The Indiana report adds a reason to require validation in each environment before transferring a correction. Its reported errors are regression-fit statistics for an adapted input channel, and the outstanding independent review can refine that interpretation. The coastal field report could supply a direct paired-site comparison. The South Florida acquisition failure supplies no scientific result. No additional search is necessary while those reports are pending.

The independent reviews of the Albemarle Sound original support using raw daily readings to flag regional episodes. They also establish that the reported inland pattern used study-wide averages and regional reference stations. The Addis Ababa spatial statistic likewise used an unsigned comparison of hourly optical readings. These findings narrow the defensible comparison to episode timing pending local validation. The West Philadelphia filter comparison quantifies daily accuracy under its sampled conditions. In Indiana, the same adjustment changed regression-fit error in opposite directions across counties, and percentage error followed a different pattern. Those findings make validation at both city sites necessary. Further literature cannot measure the offsets of these particular units or the uncertainty of their daily difference.

A fresh reading of both originals confirmed those limits, and a separate reader is checking the contrasting Indiana results. The pending South Florida and Addis Ababa originals can determine whether actual simultaneous reference contrasts support daily spatial rankings. Another search would duplicate work.

Keep the coastal field investigation open for its report on whether a network checked the signed daily difference against references at both sites. That result could tell the city which spatial comparisons a validated network can resolve. The Addis Ababa methods review confirms that its hourly spatial statistic squares the difference between optical readings and discards the sign. The Indiana review also changes how to use that campaign: the adapted correction improved the reported regression fit in one county and worsened it in another, while percentage error moved in the opposite direction. Check signed bias and daily difference error in each environment before adopting a correction. The Beijing field series supports screening for broad temporal episodes under comparable conditions. Publish the bounded West Philadelphia interpretation because the matched weighed filters provide a direct daily test of the humidity correction for that unit. The Peñuelas replicates also support repeating the side-by-side check during deployment. The published studies already cover these points, so a further search would duplicate work while the coastal report is pending.

modules.expected_delivery: Find and read the original Barkjohn, Gantt and Clements United States-wide PurpleAir PM2.5 correction field study or a comparable 24-hour reference collocation study. Extract its paired daily bias/error before and after correction, validation design, instrument, sample/sites, humidity range/limits and reference types from methods/results passages, including the stable DOI. Establish what a city could transfer and what requires local checks. Record exact evidence for the principal number and applicability; release original article and acquisition references. Treat search hits as leads.

Find an independent original field study comparing low-cost optical PM2.5 units at multiple sites or in a humid/fog/coastal setting. Prioritize simultaneous collocated replicate and reference results, conditions affecting cross-site transfer, and whether within-site temporal changes were tracked. Look for measured agreement, slope or bias under different RH or aerosol conditions and the actual averaging interval. A direct coastal and inland comparison would be especially informative. Exclude the Barkjohn national correction as the primary source for this assignment. Extract numeric and contextual passages and supply original DOI/artifact, study scope and limitations.

Independently check the two released source extractions against the supplied originals, using gx_read_source and gx_review_evidence for each. Return both review_refs. Check the West Philadelphia 24-hour error statistic, raw/corrected PM output channels, RH, seasons, comparator and independence. Check the Peñuelas RH exclusion, unit of exclusions, inter-unit precision and reference data availability. Determine whether either study measured the error in a simultaneous daily coastal-minus-inland difference. Use the existing full text.

Independently review the two released Indiana extractions using the original 24-hour field measurements and gx_review_evidence for each. Confirm the comparator, sample and site coverage, and input channel versus original US-wide formula. Assess whether opposite changes in RMSE across counties justify checking correction transfer at both local sites and whether any daily between-site ranking error was measured. Report both review_refs and consequential limitations. Existing full text is sufficient.

effective_decisions.rationale: A targeted search for the named PurpleAir national correction study can identify an open original with paired daily sensor and reference data under differing humidity conditions.

Two literature investigations are in flight. The daily reference comparisons can quantify error after correction, while an independent field deployment can test whether collocated units track changes and whether their response transfers across environments. The city supplied no collocation data of its own. I will assess the original results and their field conditions before drawing a ranking conclusion.

Find original field comparisons with site-specific reference data, then inspect the averaging interval, between-unit precision and response to humidity or aerosol conditions in their methods and results.

The first page identified the requested Barkjohn, Gantt and Clements study as DOI 10.5194/amt-14-4617-2021 and PMC8422884, with an empty fetchable_pmcids list. Search for an open original with paired 24-hour PurpleAir and reference observations, correction performance and humidity coverage.

The first catalogue page contains few field comparisons with an identifiable reference instrument. A search that requires coastal or fog conditions in the title or abstract, and a second search for original multisite evaluations, can identify studies with paired instruments and site-specific responses.

The targeted catalogue record identifies Barkjohn, Gantt and Clements (DOI 10.5194/amt-14-4617-2021, PMC8422884) and lists no fetchable original. Two accessible validation studies can test the daily comparison directly. The Philadelphia study evaluates hourly and daily observations and the Indiana study tests a national correction in two communities with different particle sources. Their original methods and result tables will determine which comparisons share a daily basis and whether the reported errors generalize between sites.

The coastal search returned three distinct open field studies in Lomé, northeastern North Carolina and Peñuelas. Their original methods and results can establish which monitors shared an inlet area with a reference, how long the averages were, and whether humidity or particle composition changed the calibration across sites.

A direct check of the sign of a daily difference between reference sites would help interpret the ongoing studies of daily accuracy and colocated precision. A targeted search can locate such a check at low cost.

West Philadelphia provides a verified 24-hour raw-to-corrected comparison under moderate spring and summer humidity. The candidate page also contains an open primary study explicitly evaluating high RH. Its methods and validation results can establish which parts of the correction transfer to the city's humid site and whether across-site performance differs from performance on held-out days. The named Barkjohn original is indexed in the first search but lacks a fetchable JATS accession in this catalogue.

Puerto Rico directly measured week-to-week replicate agreement and failure in high humidity. In North Carolina daily raw PM2.5 tracked regional AQS variability, and corrected concentrations were generally higher farther inland, but the three AQS monitors were about 50 miles from central Albemarle Sound. Lomé imported an Accra calibration on assumptions about source mix and climatology. Direct colocated reference results would resolve how far interunit precision and regional daily tracking can support quantitative site comparisons. The two selected originals investigate humidity and particle-size effects. A focused search probes whether daily calibration transfer was directly tested.

The West Philadelphia study paired daily sensor readings with a collocated gravimetric sampler and found substantially lower error after humidity correction. The coastal North Carolina study tracked daily variation against regional reference stations roughly 50 miles away, which leaves local differences unverified. In Peñuelas, humidity screening removed different fractions of each monitor’s record, and the planned regulatory comparison was unavailable. Keep the targeted search for simultaneous between-site reference differences and await the two source reports. Those results can change the scope of a defensible ranking or supply a field estimate of its uncertainty. The published daily collocation result warrants independent review when the extraction is released.

The Indiana 24-hour filter study found that applying the same correction to the PurpleAir atmospheric output reduced error in industrial Lake County and increased it in suburban Tippecanoe County. The search snapshot identifies an Addis Ababa deployment with beta attenuation monitors at two contrasting sites and a South Florida campaign comparing an inland sugarcane region with the coast. Read both originals to establish whether either verified simultaneous site differences, how humidity and aerosol sources were handled, and which comparisons had independent reference coverage. A separate reviewer is checking the West Philadelphia daily error and Peñuelas humidity exclusions.

The Beijing original shows an RH-dependent change in hourly bias below 75 µg/m³, with a reference roughly 2 km away. The Fort Collins same-rooftop original measures replicate error and bias simultaneously, and the coastal North Carolina study compares daily trends to regional monitors. A retrieved high-humidity calibration candidate can test whether a model retained accuracy on independent wet days or sites. A targeted search for experiments that explicitly transferred calibrations between measurement sites can also identify a paired-site field comparison covering both environments.
